description.narrative:
Insatsen är ett tre-årigt stöd till institutionell utveckling av den nya vattenmyndigheten vilken omfattar: - Myndighetens interna funktioner; kapacitetsutveckling genom utbildning och "on-the-job-coaching", framtagande av affärsplan/strategisk planering, utveckling av beslut och kommunikationsstrukturer, stärka förmåga att arbeta med jämställdhet och andra "cross-cutting issues". - Myndighetens externa funktioner: utveckla stratgisk kommunikationsplan för ökat genomslag/inflytande hos beslutsfattare och nyckelaktörer relevanta för vattenresursområdet (andra ministerier, kommuner, vattenkommitteer m fl). - Ökad medvetenhet bland allmänhet, näringsliv, utbildningsväsendet m fl om vattenfrågans betydelse: kampanjer för vattenresurshushållning, utveckla hemsida för allmänhetens inrapportering av illegala miljöstörande verksamheter, utveckla digital lösning/hemsida för allmänhetes ökade insyn och påverkan i beslutsfattandet.
Ansvariga albanska partners kommer att upphandla en konsult för att bistå vattenmyndigheten i genomförandet till en uppskattad kostnad av 19.7 MSEK.

The contribution involves a 3-year support to the institutional strengthening of the newly established Water Resources and Management Agency (WRMA), including: - WRMA's internal functions: capacity building through formal trainings and on-the-job coaching, development of a business plan/strategic plan, establishing functional decision-making and communication structures, strengthen WRMA's capability to work on gender equality and other cross-cutting issues. - WRMA's external functions: develop a strategic communication plan for increased impact and influence towards decision-makers and key stakeholders relevant for water resources management (other line ministries, municipalities, different water bodies etc). - Increased awarenes among the general public, private sector and education system of the importance of sustainable management of water resources: water campaigns for increasing awareness, development of website for the public to be able to report illegal activites affecting the water resource, developing digital solutions/website for increasing transparency and influence about the decision-making related to water resources.

The objective is to transform the the Albanian Water Resources Management Agency, WRMA (AMBU) into a fully functional, effective and efficient institution capable of fulfilling its legal functions and obligations. Concretely WRMA will develop a business plan/strategy for the coming 5 years and further develop work procedures, decision-making and communication structures as well as job descriptions.
WRMA aims to strengthen its capacity to work with external stakeholders and decision-makers in order to have more impact and to strengthen cross-cutting issues like gender equality, conflict and climate change. A gender policy for recruitment, retention and promotion in line with performance and merits will be developed.
Further WRMA plans to strengthen communication and engagement with key external stakeholders like the Prime Minister's Office, National Water Council, line ministries, local governments etc.
The project aims to increase the the public's awareness about sustainable water use through information campaigns and enable the public's reporting of illegal activities which threaten water resources.

The project has delivered all the agreed outputs and products, and there is already some evidence that AMBU is implementing them in its day to day function. The over arching objective was to prepare AMBU to assume its role under the new Albanian Water Resources Law and Marine Strategy Law and to help AMBU to become fit for purpose with a view to Albania's EU accession. The project developed a new organizational structure, a business plan/strategy for the coming 5 years, developed work procedures, decision making and communication structures and job descriptions as was planned, all of which contributed to fulfilling the objective.
The new organizational structure contains 106 staff, and by the time of writing most positions have been filled and are financed by the national budget. The Business Plan identifies ten strategic priorities that collectively address Albania's most pressing water management challenges and institutional development goals. These include improving water governance, ensuring equitable access to water and sanitation, advancing climate resilience and adaptation, modernizing infrastructure, promoting datadriven decision making, strengthening public awareness, and enhancing transboundary water cooperation. Each priority is underpinned by a set of measurable actions with clear time lines, responsible units, and cost estimates.
The project also aimed at strengthening AMBUs capacity to work with external stakeholders and decision makers and to strengthen crosscutting issues. Here the development of the Gender Equality Policy deserves special mentioning, being the first gender policy of an Albanian institution it has already served as a model for other institutions who are developing their own. An unexpected result under this component was the framework agreement on cross border water cooperation that was signed between Kosovo and Albania.
The project also worked on AMBUs relation to the water users and developed a system for permitting and monitoring in close cooperation with AKUK.
The project contributed to increasing the the public awareness about sustainable water use. In addition to a broad range of awareness raising activities and campaigns undertaken, the project also developed an app for reporting and monitoring illegal activities in river basins, by the public ad civil society. The function is integrated on AMBUs new webpage which the project also helped develop.
Finally the project helped AMBU develop a system for monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) which includes Key Performance Indicators for AMBU
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
